info.title: aiscast API
info.description:
Live AIS data from openwaters.io: current vessel positions, receiving stations, usage stats, self-serve tokens, and HTTP ingest for feeders. Successful responses are JSON; errors and `/health` are plain text. CORS is open, times are UTC, and JSON is compressed (zstd or gzip) when the request sends `Accept-Encoding`.

The streams are documented separately: `/v0/stream` (WebSocket, aisstream.io-compatible), `/v1/stream` (WebSocket JSON frames, MQTT over WebSocket for feeders, or Server-Sent Events), `/v1/nmea` (WebSocket, raw NMEA), and raw NMEA ingest on UDP port 10110. `/mcp` is the MCP (Model Context Protocol) endpoint for AI assistants: Streamable HTTP, no sign-in, the same tiers as `/v1/vessels`. See [openwaters.io/api/ais](https://openwaters.io/api/ais/).

tags.name: Authentication
tags.description: Create a token over HTTP. Feeder, peer, partner, and admin tokens are issued by the operator.

tags.name: Vessels and stations
tags.description: The current picture, for a map or a lookup. No token needed, 120 requests per minute per address. A token can carry its own limit. For continuous updates, use a stream instead of polling.

tags.name: Contributing
tags.description: Send what your receiver hears. Everything you feed is credited to your station, and 1,000 messages a day earns a personal token the feeder tier.

tags.name: Status
tags.description: For status pages and monitors. No token needed.

get.description:
Vessel positions as a GeoJSON FeatureCollection of `Point` features. Filter to an area, a list of vessels, or both. The same token, area cap, and MMSI cap apply as to a `/v1/stream` subscription: anonymous requests must filter to at most 100 square degrees or 10 MMSIs, and only tokens without an area claim may omit both. Properties AIS marks "not available" are left out rather than set to a sentinel, so `cog`, `sog`, `heading`, `nav_status`, `name`, and `type` are present only when known.

An area answers with last known positions: every vessel heard in it in the last 30 minutes, and those last heard up to 7 days ago whose last report was stationary, meaning moored, at anchor, aground, under 1 knot, or an aid to navigation or base station. A vessel is usually still where it stopped when its receiver goes offline or it switches AIS off at its berth, while one last heard under way has moved on. `max_age` changes the 7 days and `max_age_moving` the 30 minutes for moving vessels. Past 30 minutes the answer takes at most 500 vessels, newest first, and sets `truncated` when there were more. A vessel named in `mmsi` answers with its last known position however long ago it was heard, moving or not, unless `max_age` or `max_age_moving` is given. The vector tiles answer by the same rules. Every feature carries `seen`, so an old position reads as where the vessel was.

`q` searches instead: vessels whose name starts with it, or whose MMSI does when it is digits, most recently heard first, at most 50. Each result carries `near`, the town or region nearest its position. `around` orders a search nearest first. `bbox`, `mmsi`, and `max_age` narrow a search, and it needs neither. `kind`, `class`, `type`, `min_sog`, and `max_age_moving` filter an area, a list, or a search, as they filter the vector tiles. A search refuses parameters it does not know, so a filter added later never changes an earlier answer.

parameters.name: max_age
parameters.description: Oldest last report to include: whole seconds, a duration such as `90m` or `24h`, or `all`. Defaults to 7 days for an area and to `all` for vessels named in `mmsi`.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Search: a name prefix, case-insensitive, or an MMSI prefix when all digits. At least 2 characters.

parameters.name: around
parameters.description: `lat,lon`. Orders a search by distance from this point, nearest first, before the cap of 50 cuts it. Search only.

503.description: A search on a server running without the vessel record.

get.description: One vessel's last known state as a GeoJSON Feature, however long ago it was heard: position, course, speed, status, and the particulars from its static data. `geometry` is `null` for a vessel whose position was never heard. `first_seen` is the earliest report of the vessel the network holds, from live traffic or its archive. `attribution` carries the credit line for the source of its last message. `properties.particulars` holds the vessel's particulars as registered, merged from the enrichment sources into one vocabulary, with `properties.provenance` naming each field's source and `properties.sources` carrying each source's credit, license, and its page for this vessel.

parameters.name: mmsi
parameters.description: The vessel's MMSI.

attribution.description: Credit line for the source kind of the vessel's last message, keyed as in a FeatureCollection.

provenance.description: The source of each `particulars` field, by the field's name; values are keys of `sources`.

sources.description: Each contributing enrichment source's credit, license, and where its record is: the source's page for this vessel, or its public search when it keeps no per-vessel pages.

404.description: No vessel with this MMSI has been heard.

get.description: The positions the network heard from one vessel, as a GeoJSON Feature or a GPX 1.1 track. A request covers up to 366 days. Positions implying an impossible speed for the vessel (a report whose timestamp disagrees with its fix, a broken GPS) are left out of the track; the live stream and archive keep them. The geometry is a `LineString` for two or more positions, a `Point` for one, and `null` for none. Properties hold the range covered and arrays aligned with the coordinates: `times`, `sog`, `cog`, `heading`, and `nav_status`, with `null` where AIS marks a value not available. Without `interval` the track is simplified by shape: the positions that hold its path, at least 15 m off the line through those kept, with `breaks` naming the positions that start a stretch after the vessel went unheard, and a GPX file has a segment per stretch. With `interval`, when more positions match than the limit, the newest are returned and `truncated` is true; page back by moving `to`. `from` and `to` in the answer say what was covered. `attribution` carries the credit line for each source kind in the track, and a GPX file carries them in its metadata description.

parameters.name: mmsi
parameters.description: The vessel's MMSI.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Start, RFC 3339. Defaults to 24 hours before `to`. At most 366 days before `to`.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: End, RFC 3339. Defaults to now.

parameters.name: interval
parameters.description: At most one position per interval, the first in each: whole seconds or a duration such as `5m`, or `0` for every position heard. Anonymous and personal requests whose range starts more than 48 hours ago have the interval rounded up to whole minutes. A range longer than 31 days keeps one position per minute at most, and the answer reports that interval. A vessel sitting still has one position every 30 minutes for each place it sat. Without it, the track is simplified by shape instead. The answer reports the interval used.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Most positions to return. Defaults to 1,000 and is capped by tier: 1,000 anonymous or with a personal token, 5,000 for feeder and above.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: `geojson`, the default, or `gpx`.

geometry.description: `LineString` of `[longitude, latitude]` positions, oldest first; `Point` for one position; `null` for none.

from.description: Start of the range covered, after clamping.

interval.description: Seconds between positions at most, as requested; `0` is every position heard. Simplified, the resolution the positions were read at.

simplified.description: The track was simplified by shape: no `interval` was asked.

tolerance_m.description: Present when simplified: every position left out lay within this many meters of where the line through those kept puts the vessel at its time. 15, or more when the limit forced it.

breaks.description: Present when simplified, empty when the vessel was heard throughout: the indexes of positions that start a stretch after it went unheard. Draw no line into them.

truncated.description: Positions were left out. Simplified, the tolerance rose past 15 m to fit `limit`, or the range held more than 50,000 positions and the oldest were not read; with `interval`, the newest `limit` were kept.

404.description: No vessel with this MMSI has been heard.

503.description: Tracks are unavailable: this server runs without ClickHouse, which holds them.

get.description: One vector tile, at the URL template that `/v1/vessels/tiles.json` points to. Most maps should use the TileJSON instead. Use this template directly only for a client that takes a tile URL rather than TileJSON. It takes the same parameters and returns the same `vessels` layer. Tiles have their own rate limit of 600 requests per minute per address.

parameters.name: z
parameters.description: Zoom, 0–22. TileJSON advertises 14 as the maximum, and clients overzoom past it.

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: Column, 0 to 2^z−1.

parameters.name: y
parameters.description: Row, 0 to 2^z−1, from the north.

200.description: The tile, gzipped when the request accepts gzip. An empty tile has an empty `vessels` layer.

get.description:
Where there are vessel positions from any source, live or historical, for the last 7 complete days, UTC, as vector tiles of H3 hexagons. Point a vector source at this URL, as for the vessel tiles. A cell the network did not hear has no feature, so draw the map beneath it as it is. With `station`, the tiles are that station's cells, the tile URLs carry the parameter, `bounds` is the extent of all its cells, and `fit` frames the station without a few stray positions: each of its edges leaves out the farthest 5% of the station's finest cells on that side.

The newest day is yesterday, since today is not over. `window` gives the first and last day and how many days in between have coverage. Tiles change once a day.

```js
map.addSource("coverage", { type: "vector", url: "https://ais.openwaters.io/v1/coverage/tiles.json" });
map.addLayer({
  id: "coverage",
  type: "fill",
  source: "coverage",
  "source-layer": "coverage",
  paint: { "fill-color": "#1565c0", "fill-opacity": ["/", ["get", "days"], 7] },
});
```

#### Properties

Each cell is a polygon in the `coverage` layer, with its H3 index as the feature id. The resolution follows the zoom: 3 below zoom 5, 4 to zoom 6, 5 to zoom 8, and 6 above.

- `vessels`: distinct vessels heard in the cell a day, averaged over the window
- `days`: how many days of the window the network heard the cell at all
- `stations`: how many distinct stations heard the cell in the window. A volunteer station counts once whatever streams it tags, and each aggregator and government feed counts as one station, whatever receivers or paths it names, so a cell only one of them hears is as fragile as one heard by a single receiver.

parameters.name: station
parameters.description: A station id, as `/v1/stations` lists it. Answers that one station's cells instead of the network's: `days` counts the days the station heard the cell, `vessels` is still averaged over the window's days, and `stations` is 1.

200.description: TileJSON, with the window the tiles cover.

fit.description: With `station` only: [west, south, east, north] to frame the station by, each edge leaving out the farthest 5% of the station's finest cells on that side. `bounds` takes in every cell.

from.description: First day of the window, UTC

to.description: Last day of the window, yesterday in UTC

days.description: Days in the window the server holds coverage for, up to 7

400.description: `station` is longer than 256 characters. The body is JSON with an `error`.

404.description: The station heard nothing in the window or no station has that id, or briefly while the station's days are rebuilt. The body is JSON with an `error`.

503.description: The server has no coverage loaded: it runs without ClickHouse, or ClickHouse has no coverage for the window yet. With `station`, also when loading the station's cells failed.

get.description: One coverage tile, at the URL template that `/v1/coverage/tiles.json` points to. Most maps should use the TileJSON instead. Coverage tiles share the vessel tiles' rate limit of 600 requests per minute per address.

parameters.name: z
parameters.description: Zoom, 0–22. TileJSON advertises 10 as the maximum, and clients overzoom past it.

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: Column, 0 to 2^z−1.

parameters.name: y
parameters.description: Row, 0 to 2^z−1, from the north.

parameters.name: station
parameters.description: A station id, as `/v1/stations` lists it. Answers that one station's cells instead of the network's, with `stations` 1 in every cell.

200.description: The tile, gzipped when the request accepts gzip. A tile over water nobody heard has an empty `coverage` layer.

404.description: The station heard nothing in the window or no station has that id, or briefly while the station's days are rebuilt. The body is plain text.

503.description: The server has no coverage loaded, or with `station`, loading the station's cells failed.

get.description: Every receiving station heard since the server started, with what it contributes. `events` counts messages the station delivered first, over the last 24 hours and 7 days. `vessels` is distinct MMSIs heard in the last 30 minutes and `vessels_24h` in the last 24 hours. `vessels_exclusive_24h` counts the vessels no other station heard in those 24 hours, the gap a station fills. `bbox` is the extent of positions heard, a rough coverage footprint. Volunteer UDP stations appear as a keyed hash, never an address.
One station's statistics plus a GeoJSON FeatureCollection of the vessels it was the latest to hear. Ids can contain slashes, such as `kystverket/2573010`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Station id as reported by `/v1/stations`.

get.description: A summary for status pages and growth tracking: stations, vessels, event rates, client counts, and a breakdown by source kind. Vessel counts come from the vessel record, which holds every vessel any archive has heard. The other counts are rolling 24-hour and 7-day windows that survive restarts, never since-start totals.

post.description:
Create a personal token for an Ed25519 key you generate. It never expires. Generate a key and print its public half in the form `pubkey` expects:

```
openssl genpkey -algorithm ed25519 -out ais-key.pem
PUB=$(openssl pkey -in ais-key.pem -pubout -outform DER | tail -c 32 | base64 | tr '+/' '-_' | tr -d '=')
```

Sign the request with the same key, so nobody else can mint a token for it. The signature covers six lines joined by newlines, with no newline at the end: `aiscast-key`, `pubkey`, `ts`, `1` or `0` for `bind_ip`, `name`, and `vessel_name`, with an empty line for a name left out:

```
TS=$(date +%s)
printf 'aiscast-key\n%s\n%s\n0\n\n' "$PUB" "$TS" > msg
SIG=$(openssl pkeyutl -sign -inkey ais-key.pem -rawin -in msg | base64 | tr '+/' '-_' | tr -d '=\n')
curl -d "{\"pubkey\":\"$PUB\",\"ts\":$TS,\"sig\":\"$SIG\"}" https://ais.openwaters.io/v1/keys
```

Once a key has signed a request, every later request for it must be signed, and a request that names the station must be signed. Unsigned requests are still accepted for keys that have never signed, for clients that do not sign yet.

Tiers and limits are in [docs/limits.md](https://github.com/openwatersio/aiscast/blob/main/docs/limits.md).

pubkey.description: The raw 32-byte Ed25519 public key, base64url-encoded without padding (43 characters). Not PEM or DER.

bind_ip.description: Bind the token to the requesting address, so a receiver sending UDP from that address counts toward this token's feeder tier, and takes this request's names. The token then only works from that address.

name.description: The station's public name, up to 40 characters of letters, digits, spaces, and `. , ' - & ( ) / #`. Unique among stations. An empty string clears it. Needs `sig`. Generating again with a new name renames the station, and tokens already issued keep working.

vessel_name.description: The name of the boat the station is on, from a client that knows it, such as the Signal K plugin. Same rules as `name`, except that two stations may share it. Shown when there is no `name`. Needs `sig`.

ts.description: Unix seconds, within 5 minutes of the server clock and later than the last signed request for this key.

sig.description: Ed25519 signature by `pubkey` over the signed lines, base64url without padding.

200.description: The token and the claims it carries.

token.description: Ed25519-signed claim token, `ak1.<base64url claims>.<base64url signature>`, about 200 characters.

signed.description: `true` when the request's signature was checked and accepted. A client can wait for it before treating its key as locked to signed requests.

name_error.description: Why a requested name was not stored. The token is issued anyway.

400.description: Malformed JSON, or `pubkey` is not a base64url Ed25519 public key.

403.description: The request is not signed and must be, or its signature, `ts`, or key does not check out. The body says which.

501.description: This server has no personal-token issuer configured.

post.description:
Contributing over HTTP with AIS-catcher's `-H` output or your own client:

```
AIS-catcher -H https://ais.openwaters.io/v1/receive USERPWD x:<token> GZIP on INTERVAL 15
```

The body is AIS-catcher's `jsonaiscatcher` envelope or plain newline-separated NMEA, optionally gzipped, up to 1 MB. Needs a token, whose `sub` becomes the station name. 600 posts per minute per station. Feeding data is acceptance of the contributor agreement, linked from every response's `Link: rel="terms-of-service"` header.

rxtime.description: YYYYMMDDHHMMSS UTC; used as the message time when within 30 s of arrival.

schema.description: Newline-separated NMEA sentences, TAG blocks allowed.

413.description: Body larger than 1 MB (before or after gzip decompression).

get.description: The raw NMEA WebSocket, documented at [openwaters.io/api/ais](https://openwaters.io/api/ais/). The responses below are what a request receives when it is refused before the WebSocket upgrade.

parameters.name: bbox
parameters.description: `minLat,minLon,maxLat,maxLon`. Repeatable; boxes are ORed. Must fit inside the token's `bbox` and `area` claims.

get.description: `ok` while data is reaching subscribers. 503 after two minutes of nothing. One silent source is not an outage while the others keep the stream flowing.

text/plain.example: no events delivered to subscribers for 3m20s

200.description: The OpenAPI description of this server.

token.description: An aiscast claim token (`ak1....`), created by `POST /v1/keys` or issued by the operator. Besides `Authorization: Bearer`, the token is accepted as an HTTP Basic password (`anything:<token>`, which is what AIS-catcher's USERPWD sends) or as `?key=<token>` on the URL. A token that is present but invalid, expired, revoked, used outside its `cidr`, or lacking the role for the action is refused; it never degrades to anonymous access.

bbox.name: bbox
bbox.description: `minLat,minLon,maxLat,maxLon`. Latitude −90…90, longitude −180…180. Repeatable: the boxes are ORed and their total area counts against the token's area cap.

mmsi.name: mmsi
mmsi.description: Comma-separated MMSIs. ORed with `bbox` when both are given. An unparseable entry is a `400`.

tileMMSI.name: mmsi
tileMMSI.description: Comma-separated MMSIs: only these vessels. The MMSI cap applies, as on `/v1/vessels`.

kind.name: kind
kind.description: Comma-separated: `vessel`, `aton` (aids to navigation), `base` (base stations), `sar` (search and rescue aircraft).

class.name: class
class.description: `A` or `B`, the transponder class from the position reports. A vessel whose class is not yet known is left out.

type.name: type
type.description: Comma-separated ITU ship and cargo type codes or ranges, such as `70-89` for cargo and tankers or `36,37` for sailing and pleasure craft. For an aid to navigation, the AtoN type. A vessel whose type is not yet known is type 0.

min_sog.name: min_sog
min_sog.description: Only vessels at least this fast, in knots. A vessel with no known speed is left out.

tileMaxAge.name: max_age
tileMaxAge.description: Oldest last report to include: whole seconds, a duration such as `24h`, or `all`. Defaults to 7 days, or to `all` when `mmsi` is given.

max_age_moving.name: max_age_moving
max_age_moving.description: Oldest last report to include for a vessel whose last report was under way, that is, not stationary as `/v1/vessels` defines it: whole seconds, a duration such as `2h`, or `all`. Defaults to 30 minutes for an area and to `all` for vessels named in `mmsi`.

BadRequest.description: Malformed parameter or body. The plain-text body says which.

Unauthorized.description: Missing, invalid, expired, or revoked token, or the token lacks the role for this action. The plain-text body gives the reason.

RateLimited.description: Over the per-address or per-station request limit.

attribution.description: Credit lines to display, one per source kind present in the features. The key is a feature's `source` value up to the first `:`. Every credit opens with "Open Waters AIS (https://openwaters.io/ais/)"; sources with their own terms add their credit after it.

truncated.description: Present when a cap cut the list: a search past 50 matches, or an area past 500 vessels older than 30 minutes.

VesselFeature.description: One vessel and its last known position.

geometry.description: The last known position. Always present in a FeatureCollection; `null` from `/v1/vessels/{mmsi}` for a vessel whose position was never heard.

type.description: AIS ship/cargo code, or AtoN type. Present only when known.

cog.description: Course over ground, degrees. Present only when known.

sog.description: Speed over ground, knots. Present only when known.

heading.description: True heading, degrees. Present only when known.

nav_status.description: AIS navigational status. Present only when known.

near.description: The town or region nearest the position, such as `Santa Monica, CA` or `Munster, Ireland`. On `q` searches only, and absent more than 100 km from a town of 5,000. Place names from GeoNames, CC BY 4.0.

flag.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code of the flag state, from the MMSI's maritime identification digits. Present only when the MID is known.

imo.description: IMO number from the vessel's static data. Present only when sent.

callsign.description: Radio call sign. Present only when sent.

destination.description: Destination as typed by the crew: a port name, a UN/LOCODE, or nothing useful. Present only when sent.

eta.description: Estimated arrival as sent, `MM-DD HH:MM` UTC, or `MM-DD` when the time is not available. AIS carries no year. Present only when sent.

draught.description: Maximum static draught, metres. Present only when sent.

length.description: Overall length, metres, from the dimension fields. Present only when sent.

beam.description: Beam, metres. Present only when sent.

to_bow.description: Metres from the AIS antenna (the vessel's reference point) to the bow; 511 means 511 or more. `to_bow` and `to_stern` add up to `length` and are present together once known, and 0 can be a real value: a vessel that does not know where its antenna sits sends 0 to the bow and its length to the stern.

to_stern.description: Metres from the AIS antenna to the stern; 511 means 511 or more. Present together with `to_bow`.

to_port.description: Metres from the AIS antenna to the port side; 63 means 63 or more. `to_port` and `to_starboard` add up to `beam` and are present together once known; a vessel that does not know where its antenna sits sends 0 to port and its beam to starboard.

to_starboard.description: Metres from the AIS antenna to the starboard side; 63 means 63 or more. Present together with `to_port`.

first_seen.description: The earliest report of the vessel the network holds, from live traffic or its archive. On `/v1/vessels/{mmsi}` only.

seen.description: Time of the last message that updated the vessel.

source.description: Source of that message: an upstream name, `station:<sub>` for an authenticated contributor (whatever transport it fed over), `udp:<hash>`, or `mmsi:<n>`.

msg_type.description: aisstream-style type name of that message.

Particulars.description: Particulars as registered, merged from the enrichment sources into one vocabulary. Present on `/v1/vessels/{mmsi}` when a source knows the vessel: Wikidata by the IMO from its static data, when the IMO has a valid check digit and an item; the US Coast Guard's PSIX for a US-flag vessel whose call sign and name both match a vessel it lists; the Norwegian Directorate of Fisheries' fishing vessel register (NLOD 2.0), matched the same way for a Norwegian vessel; the FCC's ship station licenses, keyed by the MMSI itself for a US vessel; Transport Canada's vessel register (Open Government Licence - Canada), by IMO for a CA-flag vessel; and ISED's Canadian MMSI registry, asked on demand for heard CA-flag vessels. Merging is per field: a flag state outranks Wikidata for registered facts, an empty value never wins, and `provenance` beside this object names each field's source. Registered dimensions can differ from the ones AIS reports. Every field is present only when a source has it.

registered_name.description: Name as documented with the flag state, which can differ from the AIS name.

identification.description: The flag state's number for the vessel: the official number of a documented vessel, else its state registration.

service.description: Flag-state service type, such as `Towing Vessel`, `Passenger (Inspected)`, `Commercial Fishing Vessel`, or `Recreational`.

callsign.description: Call sign as registered. The `callsign` in the vessel's properties is the one AIS reports.

status.description: Flag-state status, such as `Active` or `Laid Up`.

ship_type.description: Kind of ship, such as `bulk carrier`, `container ship`, `oil tanker`, or `ferry`.

year_built.description: Year the vessel was built or entered service.

tonnage_measure.description: How a tonnage from the flag state was measured: `Convention` is the international system, `Regulatory` the older US system in register tons, and `Simplified` the method for small vessels. A Regulatory or Simplified gross tonnage is served only when no Convention figure exists.

draught.description: Design draught in meters. The `draught` in the vessel's properties is the one AIS reports for the current voyage.

former_names.description: Names the vessel carried before, oldest first.

commons_category.description: The category of the ship's photos on Wikimedia Commons. The photos carry their own licenses.

image.description: The Wikimedia Commons page of a photo of the ship, which shows the photo's license and credit and links its thumbnails.

SourceRef.description: One enrichment source's credit: how to name it and where its record of this vessel is. `sources` maps each contributing source's key, such as `wikidata`, `uscg`, `fiskeridir`, `fcc`, `tc`, or `ised`, to one of these, and `provenance` maps each `particulars` field to a key of `sources`.

license.description: The source's license. `CC0-1.0` and `public domain (U.S. government work)` require no credit line.

url.description: The source's page for this vessel, or its public search when the source keeps no per-vessel pages.

station.description: Station id. Volunteer UDP stations are a keyed hash of the sender, never an address. A feed's TAG `s:` adds a path naming one of its receivers, such as `barentswatch/terra`; a volunteer's station is its `source`, whatever its sentences' TAG `s:` says.

duplicates.description: Position messages another station delivered first, over the station's history. Up to about 7 minutes behind.

vessels.description: Distinct MMSIs whose positions the station heard in the last 30 minutes, its own vessel left out. Up to about 7 minutes behind.

vessels_24h.description: Distinct MMSIs whose positions the station heard in the last 24 hours, its own vessel left out. Up to about 7 minutes behind.

vessels_exclusive_24h.description: Of `vessels_24h`, the vessels no other station heard. A vessel counts whether this station delivered a message first or as a duplicate, and an aggregator's late copy of a report another station already delivered does not count as hearing it.

uptime_7d.description: Share of hours with a position reception, from 0 to 1, over the last 7 days or since the station's first hour if later. The current hour counts once it has one. Null until the station series has the station.

name.description: What to call the station: the name its operator chose when minting its token, else the name of the boat it is on. Absent when it has neither, or when moderation has locked it. Rows that share a station id before `/` share a name.

mmsi.description: The station's own vessel, from the `!AIVDO` sentences it sends.

near.description: The town or region nearest the traffic the station hears, such as `Santa Monica, CA` or `Munster, Ireland`. Volunteer stations only. Place names from GeoNames, CC BY 4.0.

positions.description: Position messages over the station's history. Up to about 7 minutes behind.

first_seen.description: The station's first hour in its history, or when this server first heard it if earlier or not yet in the history.

bbox.description: `[minLat, minLon, maxLat, maxLon]` extent of positions heard, a rough coverage footprint. Absent until a position has been heard.

Windows.description: A rolling counter: hourly buckets, kept across restarts.

total.description: Stations heard since the server started.

active.description: Stations heard in the last 5 minutes.

by_source.description: Station counts grouped by source kind: `station` (authenticated contributors), `udp`, `mmsi`, or the upstream name.

vessels.description: `total` and the windows count the vessel record, refreshed once a minute. `active`, `with_position`, and `by_kind` describe the vessels heard in the last 30 minutes. A server running without the record reports `total` as `active` and leaves out the windows.

total.description: Every vessel the network has heard.

active.description: Vessels heard in the last 30 minutes.

last_24h.description: Vessels heard in the last 24 hours.

last_7d.description: Vessels heard in the last 7 days.

last_30d.description: Vessels heard in the last 30 days.

new.description: Vessels first heard in each window.

per_second.description: Deduplicated event rate over the last 30 s.

sources.description: Keyed by source kind: each upstream by name, every authenticated contributor as `station`, all UDP senders as `udp`.

last_age_s.description: Seconds since any member last produced an event.

vessels.description: Distinct MMSIs heard in the last 30 minutes.

vessels_exclusive.description: Of those, MMSIs no other source kind heard in that window.

delay.description: Seconds from broadcast to arrival at aiscast over the last 512 position reports from this kind. The broadcast time is the report's UTC-second field placed in the minute of the event's canonical time, so delays of 55 s or more wrap. Absent until a position report with a valid second has been heard.

n.description: Samples in the window, at most 512.

Claims.description: The claims a token carries. Absent limits mean unlimited.

sub.description: Who: a station name, partner name, or `ed25519:<pubkey>` / `mmsi:<n>` for a device.

exp.description: Expiry, unix seconds. Absent on personal tokens, which never expire.

bbox.description: Boxes every subscription must fit inside, each `[minLat, minLon, maxLat, maxLon]`.

cidr.description: Source CIDRs/IPs the token may be used from.

rate.description: Messages per second per connection; excess is thinned.

area.description: Total subscribed bounding-box area in square degrees. Negative means MMSI-only subscriptions.

mmsis.description: Vessels followed by MMSI per subscription.
